chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara and Muhammad Bin Muslim, and Bureyd Bin Muawiya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:
Regarding the absentee when he divorces his wife, she should observe the waiting period from the day he divorces her.
ai.seo_question: When does the waiting period begin for a wife if her husband is absent and divorces her?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the iddah commences immediately upon the husband's pronouncement of divorce, even if he is absent, resolving the juristic debate on whether the wife must wait for notification. It underscores the Shia principle that the act of divorce is effective at the moment of utterance by the husband, ensuring legal certainty for the wife's status. This ruling is foundational in fiqh al--talaq, distinguishing between the validity of the divorce and the practical knowledge of it.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara and Muhammad Bin Muslim, and Bureyd Bin Muawiya, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘With regards to the absentee, when he divorces his wife, she should observe the waiting period from the day he divorces her’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn ‘Udhaynah, from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Burayd ibn Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has narrated the following: “About the case of one who is absent if he divorces his wife abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
She must commence her ‘Iddah (waiting period) from the day he has divorced her.’”
